holidays.name: Good Samaritan Involvement Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to stopping to help a stranger in need, whether that means changing a tire, carrying groceries, or simply offering a kind word. It encourages people to put down their phones and actually notice who around them could use a hand.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States as an unofficial day of kindness, inspired by the biblical parable of the Good Samaritan, in which a traveler helps a stranger who was ignored by others.
holidays.funFact: Many U.S. states have 'Good Samaritan laws' that legally protect people who step in to help in an emergency from being sued.

holidays.name: K9 Veterans Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the brave working dogs who have served in the U.S. military, sniffing out explosives, guarding bases, and saving countless human lives. Expect lots of treats and salutes for good boys and girls.
holidays.origin: Held on March 13 to mark the anniversary of the founding of the U.S. Army Canine Corps in 1942, which formally began recruiting dogs for military service during World War II.
holidays.funFact: Early in the program, the public donated pet dogs for the war effort through a campaign called 'Dogs for Defense,' and thousands of family pets were trained for service.

holidays.name: Jewel Day
holidays.description: A sparkly day for celebrating gemstones and jewelry, perfect for digging out Grandma's brooch, polishing your rings, or treating yourself to something shiny.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance popular with jewelry lovers and retailers, celebrating the beauty and history of gems and precious stones.
holidays.funFact: Diamonds are not the rarest gems on Earth; some stones like painite and red beryl were once far scarcer than diamonds.

holidays.name: Open an Umbrella Indoors Day
holidays.description: A day for fearlessly defying superstition by popping open an umbrella inside the house, tempting fate with seven years of bad luck at the ready. Bring your bravest rain gear and your sense of humor.
holidays.origin: Created as a playful challenge to a famous superstition, which is often tied to the 18th-century London invention of sturdy spring-loaded umbrellas that could injure people or knock things over indoors.
holidays.funFact: Some historians say the superstition is much older and comes from ancient Egypt, where umbrellas were parasols that shielded the sun gods and opening one indoors was thought to insult them.

holidays.name: Girls Just Wanna Have Fun Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to leaving your worries behind and having an absolutely good time, with karaoke, dancing, and friends all encouraged, preferably with a Cyndi Lauper soundtrack.
holidays.origin: An unofficial pop culture celebration inspired by Cyndi Lauper's 1983 hit song, which became an anthem of joyful independence.
holidays.funFact: The song was originally written and recorded by songwriter Robert Hazard from a male point of view, and Lauper changed the lyrics to turn it into the feminist anthem we know today.
